description: The line plot illustrates the MRR@10 (Mean Reciprocal Rank at 10) performance of various DPR (Dense Passage Retrieval) variants as a function of the number of queries used during inference (S), ranging from 1 to 10. The x-axis, labeled “Number of queries used during inference (S),” is linearly scaled from 1 to 10 with integer tick marks. The y-axis, labeled “MRR@10,” is linearly scaled from 33.0 to 36.5, with major tick marks at 0.5 intervals. Six distinct lines represent different DPR configurations: “DPR w/o query” (black solid line) starts at ~33.0 and rises sharply to ~36.4 at S=10; “DPR w/ gold” (yellow line with circle markers) begins at ~33.0 and increases steadily to ~35.0; “DPR w/ top-1” (green line with circle markers) starts at ~34.8 and climbs to ~36.4; “DPR w/ bottom-1” (purple line with circle markers) remains relatively flat around 34.8–35.0; “DPR w/ random” (blue line with circle markers) stays near 35.0–35.7; and “DPR w/ curriculum” (red line with circle markers) begins at ~35.6 and plateaus near 35.8. Two horizontal dashed lines are present: a red dashed line at ~35.6 and a green dashed line at ~34.8, likely indicating baseline or reference performance levels. All lines except “DPR w/o query” and “DPR w/ gold” show relatively stable or slowly increasing trends, while “DPR w/o query” and “DPR w/ top-1” exhibit the most significant performance gains as S increases.
